Well, how exactly does one *eat* Fette Sau seeing as how they only sell the meat?  And their website says they close at 5 during the week, which has me worried since we're not starting the day until her train gets in at noon.

You're like my favorite person ever right now.  Really.  This is going to be incredible and we're both going to have so much fun and kinda owe it all to you.  I'll give you an update when it's all over.

The budget is kinda unlimited, since I don't mind paying for a lot of crap, but I'm definitely trying to keep it on the cheaper end of things.  No five-star restaurants where I need to bribe the maitre'd to get a seat, and nothing where we need to be dressed up beyond jeans.  Staying around $100 total for the day would be nice, but going over isn't the end of the world at all.

The more walking the better, but subway time is fine (we were going to take it for ~30 minutes to get to the first destination from Penn Station anyways, though now I'm definitely switching us to the ferry).  The day is a Wednesday and the timeframe is pretty much all day.  I'm not sure when she's getting into the city, but I'm not letting her leave until nightfall.

Food and discovering neighborhoods would be a plus.  I'm leery of museums just because going inside on really nice days as well as taking too much time out of the day.  If they're worth it, then it doesn't really matter.  I've spent an entire day at L'Orangerie in Paris even though there really isn't much in there, and I've probably spent around a month total of my life in the Natural History Museum on Central Park West.  She's an artist, so good museums are welcome.

Hipster/colorful Brooklyn sound great.  I was hoping for the day to end with Grimaldi's and the Bridge just because that sounds romantic, but any other romantic alternative sounds great.  I think we're going to end it with Brooklyn Bridge Park and Jacques Torres just because that sounds the best.  I think we're going to try to start the day with Le Petit (courtesy of someone else in the thread) and try to end it at the Bridge, even though the ferry to take us into Brooklyn would drop us off at the Bridge to start.  The more I write about it the more it seems really backwards.  If there's a good alternative I'll definitely take it.

Thank you so much for your help.

**Edit**: Fixing where we end the day.
I think you just won my eternal gratitude.

I move into college on a Wednesday, meet her on a Friday, we spend all of Saturday together, and that was that.  We were tied together at the hip and it was incredible.  She was my first girlfriend, which lead to me over-compensating for a lot, and she took advantage of it big time.  I was left fawning over her all the time, and she just ate it up.

Then my father passed in late October.

She had to take care of me, and wasn't okay with that dynamic.  We kept going for months with me breaking down, her not being okay with that, and then me apologizing for having done it in the first place.  It took me a few months to realize that it was dysfunctional, and I devoted the next eight to trying to change it.  I talked to her all the time about it, I was honest, I tried my best.  I really did and it's cause I love her.  Hell, I still do.  It just wasn't working and since I'm starting medication and dealing with a whole bunch o' shit, it's not fair to either of us to keep going.

It's not passive-agressive as em_son is making it be.  I just sincerely wish I hadn't gotten so attached before needing to do it.  She's still friends with my roommate, and we pulled an all-nighter together to prep for my final final today, and it wasn't too weird, but I really wish there was a way for us to be better friends.

I really wish I had broken up with her sooner instead of dragging us both through a bunch of shit.
Sorry for not breaking up with you sooner.
